what_this_is: Magnetics (mag-inc) powder-core toroid data: physical geometry and AL per permeability, transcribed from the vendor catalog. It is a transcription of printed tables, not a model.

source.vendor: Magnetics, a Division of Spang & Company
source.extraction: PyMuPDF text words. Column assignment uses the x position of the nine material column headers on each page (Kool Mu, Kool Mu MAX, Kool Mu Hf, Kool Mu Ultra, XFlux, XFlux Ultra, Edge, High Flux, MPP), not token order, because the catalog drops cells that are empty.

units.al_nh: nH/T^2 found in the table body

part_number_reading.layout: GradingCode(2) + MaterialCode(2) + CatalogNumber(3) + CoreFinish(2), e.g. C055206A2

grading_code.00: not graded, AL is printed as a single value with the +-8% band stated above the column
grading_code.C0: graded into narrower inductance bands, see al_tolerance_pct_c0

part_number_reading.material_code: the two digits after the grading code; this is what the nine columns carry, and it is used here as an independent cross-check that the column assignment is right

core_finish.A2: 2000 VAC min wire-to-wire (varies by OD), High Flux / Edge / MPP only
core_finish.A7: 2000 VAC min (varies by OD), Kool Mu family and XFlux family
core_finish.AY: 600 VAC min, Parylene-C, OD 3.56-16.6 mm, not available for 550u MPP

al_tolerance_pct_c0.rule: MPP and High Flux cores with a C0 prefix and OD > 4.65 mm are graded into 2% inductance bands; MPP cores with a C0 prefix and OD 4.65 mm and smaller are graded into 5% bands.

material_comparison_printed_page_10.what_this_is: the vendor own nine-column comparison table on printed p.10, transcribed by column x position; the same page that the loss fits were cross-checked against in 0.0.75
material_comparison_printed_page_10.the_saturation_row_is_the_one_to_use_for: printed p.10 gives one saturation number per material column, with no temperature and no tolerance; that is what a DC-bias verdict should be judged against, and it is the only page in this catalog that prints a saturation number for MPP
material_comparison_printed_page_10.asterisks: the catalog marks some cells with a star (e.g. Ultra 100 mW/cc, Edge 130 Oe, High Flux 130 Oe, Kool Mu 1x*); the star points at a footnote that this transcription does not carry, so those cells are copied with the star

material_properties_printed_page_16.what_this_is: Curie temperature, density at 60u, coefficient of thermal expansion per material column, and the factors that relate a 60u density to the other permeabilities - printed on p.16
material_properties_printed_page_16.density_basis: grams/cm3 for the 60u permeability of that column; a pressed powder core carries binder, so this is the core bulk density and not the alloy density
material_properties_printed_page_16.weight_is_an_estimate: the catalog says See individual data sheets for nominal core weights, so a mass computed from Ve x density x factor is an estimate, not the vendor nominal weight
material_properties_printed_page_16.permeabilities_without_a_printed_factor_: p.16 prints eleven factors for fourteen permeabilities; 200u, 300u and 550u have none, so a mass for those is refused rather than interpolated

cells.a_part_number: that material is offered in this size at this permeability
cells.a_dash: the catalog prints a dash: not offered
cells.null: the catalog prints nothing at all in this cell (the cell is blank, which is why token order cannot be used to read this table)

printing_anomalies.why: this is a High Flux part number (material code 58) printed in the MPP column, identical to the High Flux cell in the same row; the MPP part number is missing. Kept verbatim, confirmed on the rendered page.
printing_anomalies.verified_by: rendered page image, not only the text layer

printing_anomalies.why: this is a High Flux part number (material code 58) printed in the Edge column, identical to the High Flux cell in the same row; the Edge part number is missing. Kept verbatim, confirmed on the rendered page.
printing_anomalies.verified_by: rendered page image, not only the text layer

printing_anomalies.why: the second character is the letter O in the PDF content stream, not the digit zero; every other graded part number on the same pages uses the digit zero. Visually the two are indistinguishable, so a buyer must be told. Kept verbatim.
printing_anomalies.verified_by: text-layer character code, compared against the other C0 cells on the same page

printing_anomalies.why: the vendor own three numbers are mutually inconsistent: 492 x 177.2 = 87,182, and 81,500 / 177.2 = 460. Ae is confirmed independently (0.989 of the rectangular cross-section HT*(OD-ID)/2), Le is confirmed independently (log-mean pi*(OD-ID)/ln(OD/ID) = 177.19). So the printed Ve is the odd one out by 6.5%. All three are stored verbatim; nothing was corrected.
printing_anomalies.verified_by: rendered page image plus two independent geometric checks

printing_anomalies.why: the same High Flux part number is printed again on printed p.168 (pdf p.169) against a different size (OD 16.59 mm, perm 40 u). A catalog number encodes the size and the AL, so one part number cannot be right for two sizes; the catalog does not say which cell is the wrong one, so both rows are kept verbatim and neither part number is invented. Found by counting distinct part numbers against distinct cells (1923 cells, 1920 distinct).
printing_anomalies.verified_by: both pages rendered and read as images; the text layer agrees with the images on both pages
